newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Greens to oppose social cuts - source.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Greens to oppose social cuts - source.

text.p: The two Australian Greens senators will oppose social security measures from the government's budget worth about A$700 million over three years, a parliamentary source said on Friday.
The Greens are scheduled to formally announce their plans at an 0130 GMT (11.30 a.m. AEST) news conference.

The source, familiar with the Greens' plans, did not specify the particular items that the Greens would oppose, but no social security measures are in doubt because every one of them is expected to get the backing of either the Labor opposition or the Australian Democrats minor party.

Major spending measures announced in the August 20 budget include making migrants wait two years for social security, saving about A$360 million in the three years to June 1999, and the introduction of tighter tests for unemployment benefits, saving about A$260 million in that time.
The government needs the support of at least two non-government senators to get budget measures through the Senate, the upper house of parliament.
Those votes can come from the Greens, Labor, the Democrats or a pair of Independents.
